newsitem.title: INDIA: India fixes support price for summer wheat crop.
newsitem.headline: India fixes support price for summer wheat crop.

text.p: The Indian government has fixed the procurement price for the summer wheat crop at 4,150 rupees per tonne, up from 3,800 rupees in the previous season, a Food Ministry statement said on Wednesday.

The statement quoted Food Secretary S.P. Jakhanwal as saying at a meeting of food secretaries of wheat producing states that sufficient purchase centres should be opened for wheat procurement, starting from April.
India expects a wheat crop of about 64 million tonnes in 1996/97 (October-September) against 62.3 millon tonnes in 1995/96. A clear picture should emerge by early February.
Government wheat procurement in the 1995/96 growing season fell to 8.2 million tonnes from 12.3 million tonnes in the previous year due to a three-million-tonne shortfall in output.
